card.flavorText: The Fiat G.50 Freccia ("Arrow") was an Italian fighter aircraft which was used by the Regia Aeronautica (the Italian Air Force) and their allies during WWII. When it entered service in 1938, it was widely regarded as being an extremely maneuverable aircraft and was often considered to be one of Italy's best fighters. In November 1939 Finland purchased 35 Fiat G.50s from Italy. Only fourteen were delivered by the end of the "Winter War". All thirty-five had arrived and were ready for service by the time the "Continuation War" started and they were assigned to Lentolaivue 26 (Flying Squadron 26), where they replaced the squadron's aging Fokker XXIs and Gloster Gladiators. The G.50s were in service until they were replaced in May 1944 by Brewster Buffalos. The G.50 proved to be an effective fighter in the hands of Finnish pilots who achieved a remarkable kill/loss ratio of 33 to 1.
